dataset.role: Comparative chart benchmarks & pedagogical parameter uncertainty illustration

retail_consumption.model: Retail Sales YoY ~ Unemployment Rate (Contemporaneous OLS)
retail_consumption.role: Contemporaneous descriptive historical association among landmark years. NOT an identified causal policy effect or validated 12-month predictive forecast.

recession_classifier.model: Recession Indicator ~ Fed Funds Rate + Unemployment Rate (Logistic MLE)
substantive_limitations: Small sample size (N=16 total landmark years, with only 4 recession events: 2001, 2008, 2009, 2020).
High estimation uncertainty: Neither policy rate (p=0.772) nor unemployment (p=0.160) reaches statistical significance at alpha=0.05.
Selected landmark snapshots chosen to illustrate cyclical extremes; not sampled uniformly or continuously.
NBER target definition is determined retrospectively; fitting on annual landmark snapshots does not establish prospective forecasting capability.
Absence of prospective temporal validation: Model has not been validated on rolling out-of-time splits or untouched holdout cycles.

fit_results.model: Retail Sales YoY ~ Unemployment Rate (Contemporaneous OLS)
fit_results.role: Contemporaneous descriptive historical association among landmark years. NOT an identified causal policy effect or validated 12-month predictive forecast.

retail_consumption.caveats: Contemporaneous descriptive association. Not an identified causal policy effect or validated 12-month forecast.

labor_market_transmission.classification: Illustrative Policy Assumption / Calibrated Sensitivity Rule

assumed_parameters.interpretation: +0.15pp unemployment per 100bps Fed Funds rate deviation above 2.5%

labor_market_transmission.rationale: Non-consecutive landmark years contain multi-year gaps (up to 5 years between 2010 and 2015) with only 11 consecutive 1-year pairs. Dynamic annual lag regressions cannot be defensibly identified without a continuous annual panel. Retained as an illustrative policy sensitivity heuristic.

inflation_persistence_drag.classification: Illustrative Policy Assumption / Calibrated AR-X Sensitivity

assumed_parameters.interpretation: Fraction 0.65 inflation persistence carried forward minus 0.08pp drag per 1pp Fed rate

inflation_persistence_drag.rationale: Multi-year gaps violate lag-1 dynamic assumptions. Retained as an illustrative simulation heuristic.

substantive_limitations: Small sample size (N=16 total landmark years, with only 4 recession events: 2001, 2008, 2009, 2020).
High estimation uncertainty: Neither policy rate (p=0.772) nor unemployment (p=0.160) reaches statistical significance at alpha=0.05.
Selected landmark snapshots chosen to illustrate cyclical extremes; not sampled uniformly or continuously.
NBER target definition is determined retrospectively; fitting on annual landmark snapshots does not establish prospective forecasting capability.
Absence of prospective temporal validation: Model has not been validated on rolling out-of-time splits or untouched holdout cycles.

recession_indicator.caveats: Empirically fitted to the 16 landmark snapshots (LL = -7.2199, pseudo-R² = 0.1976). Not an independently validated prospective forecasting model; large standard errors reflect small-sample limitations.

methodological_distinctions.parameter_uncertainty: SE(beta) describes sampling standard deviation of coefficient estimators.
methodological_distinctions.conditional_mean_interval: mu_hat(x) +- t * s_e * sqrt(1/n + (x - x_bar)^2 / SS_xx). Uncertainty of the expected average response.
methodological_distinctions.forecast_prediction_interval: y_new +- t * s_e * sqrt(1 + 1/n + (x - x_bar)^2 / SS_xx). Substantially wider due to individual residual variance s_e^2.
methodological_distinctions.recession_mle_classification: Empirically fitted in-sample via MLE on 16 landmark snapshots. Due to small sample size (4 events) and selection of turning points, it is NOT an out-of-sample validated probability forecast.
methodological_distinctions.lag_structure_limitation: Multi-year gaps (up to 5 years between 2010 and 2015) violate uniform annual lag assumptions (t -> t+1). Continuous annual series is required for valid dynamic lag estimation.
